title: Prajāpati, none but you encompasses all these

sandhi_exceptions.note: नो अस्तु: -aḥ becomes -o and the following a is kept, as the Saṃhitā and the Ṛgveda write it.

words.meaning: has been; with pari, has encompassed
words.role: main verb of the first line

sandhi.rule: -t before a vowel becomes -d; -i before a vowel becomes -y; -aḥ before a voiced consonant becomes -o
a visarga before t becomes s

samasa.meaning: whose desire is what (that for which we long)

morphology.note: neuter plural in -ā for later विश्वानि (Sāyaṇa: «शेश्छन्दसि बहुलम्»).

translation.literal: Prajāpati, no other than you has encompassed all these born things; with whatever desire we offer to you, may that be ours; may we be lords of riches.
translation.readable: Prajāpati, none other than you encompasses all that has been born. What we desire as we offer to you, may it be ours; may we be lords of riches.

meaning: The last verse of the hymn to the unknown god (RV 10.121.10), which names him at the end as Prajāpati, lord of creatures; also in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā (1.8.14.2). No one but Prajāpati encompasses all that is born; may the wish with which we offer to him be fulfilled, and may we be lords of riches. Sāyaṇa takes ‘encompass’ as ‘grasp and create’: only Prajāpati can hold all beings and bring them forth. The verse addresses Prajāpati.
in_the_rite: The second mantra of Śanaiścara’s step in the Navagraha sūktam (witness S). S names the adhidevatā and pratyadhidevatā together, so the edition does not say which this verse is for; the verse itself addresses Prajāpati. Its use for a graha belongs to the later gṛhya tradition.

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Sāyaṇa, on the Ṛgveda: no other grasps or pervades these beings — «त्वमेवैतानि परिगृह्य स्रष्टुं शक्नोषीति भावः», ‘you alone can hold them and create them’.

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Bhāskara, on the Saṃhitā: Prajāpati pervades all beings «निजेन महिम्ना», by his own greatness; and the prayer is for the wish with which we offer, and to be lords of riches always.

notes.label: linguistic
notes.text: A triṣṭubh; one hiatus (नो अस्तु) is kept as the Saṃhitā writes it.
